definitions.meaning: people who try or taste something, as at a food stall, are those who sample it
embroidered cloths that show off a range of stitches, often worked by girls in past centuries

explanation.surface: Folk having a go at sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters who try things sample them, and an embroidered display cloth of stitches is also called by this name.

parts.note: a phrase meaning to cancel, which is also the formal legal term a judge uses when quashing a verdict

explanation.surface: Cancelling something, even where a judge presides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' tempts a tennis reading (sets, sides), but the clue means a law court: the phrase is the term for a judge quashing a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a judgment or order is the legal idiom here, used by appeal judges quashing earlier rulings.

clue.text: Lot of animals, people agree-I differ

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for people

indicators.note: the letters of agree and I differ from their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone disagreeing with a crowd about a collection of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differ' rearranges AGREEI into AGERIE, which follows MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild beasts kept for show is a zoo-like gathering of creatures.

indicators.note: breaking the letters into pieces and putting them back together signals the rearrangement

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Solo piano compositions that include running passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' rearranges SOLE plus P into the answer; 'containing' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, loping stride is an easy bounding run, so it runs in that relaxed way.

parts.note: rye is a cereal grain
a peck is an old dry measure of two gallons

explanation.surface: A Polish trader provides a quantity of corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is the definition, a punting post.
explanation.definitionFit: A rye-peck is an iron-shod stake driven into a riverbed to moor a punt, a kind of post.

annotationWithheld.why: Good fellows left aboard, apparently: S(PORT)S, but 'aboard' must give both the SS (steamship) letters and the containing operation, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Music said to get in the dough

annotationWithheld.why: Music said to get in the dough: a homophone of some phrase for 'get in the dough', but no reading of the phrase sounds clearly like PASTORALE
annotationWithheld.clue: Music said to get in the dough

indicators.note: the letters of hard and o could do something else, being rearranged into a new order

parts.note: o, the zero figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A young woman able to do nothing difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could do' rearranges HARD plus O (nothing) into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female given name, and crosswords freely use any girl's name for a girl.

clue.text: Someone nigh on burning to entertain us ?

definitions.meaning: a person who scorches something lightly, all but burning it
a performer whose voice entertains an audience

explanation.surface: A person close to catching fire who still performs for us.
explanation.walkthrough: To singe is to burn slightly, so one who singes is 'nigh on burning'; the same word names a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching lightly is singeing, so the doer is named by that verb, which also names a vocal performer.

clue.text: Soldier appears to request change of air

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: a change of the letters of air rearranges them

explanation.surface: A soldier seems to want some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges AIR into ARI, after ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari is a native East African soldier in colonial service.

clue.text: Music interval with American writer's work

parts.note: a tone is a musical interval of two semitones
Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
MS, manuscript, is a writer's work

explanation.surface: A musical gap combined with the output of a US author.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral piece in one movement that tells a story or paints a scene is a kind of music.

definitions.meaning: an old wooden golf club with a lofted face, one member of the set of clubs
a piece of cutlery that carries food during a meal

explanation.surface: A member of a society keeps on munching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club member' suggests a member of a society; it is a golf club in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The utensil carries soup to the mouth, and an old lofted golf club had the same name.

parts.note: read literally, a person breathes out air in a way that shows sorrow

explanation.surface: Someone gives off a melancholy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like an atmosphere or manner, but it is literal breath let out sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Long sad breaths let out audibly are exactly air expelled in sorrow.

clue.text: Vanish with girl quietly, so to speak

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Disappearing quietly alongside a young woman, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid turning to vapour disappears, so the word is used for anything that vanishes.

clue.text: Crane is of the German strain

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
to rick is to strain or wrench a joint

explanation.surface: A wading bird of a German breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane' and 'strain' suggest a bird and its breed; it is a lifting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a lifting rig with a jib, a kind of crane.

definitions.meaning: what someone in a hospital bed might say to a ward sister: I am a patient

explanation.surface: An anxious hello to a nun or sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sister' is a senior hospital nurse in Britain; someone introducing themselves to one says 'I'm patient'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and unable to wait calmly is a fretful state.

parts.note: the Greek myth of the boy who flew on wax wings too near the sun, which melted them

explanation.surface: A pilot with a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun-burned' suggests a peeling tourist; it is the mythical flier whose wings the sun destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son flew with wax wings, rose too near the sun and fell, making him a doomed flier.

definitions.meaning: a workman placed above the others, a superior labourer

explanation.surface: The benefit of being the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hand' is a worker, so a foreman is a higher-placed hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a commanding position, and read literally it is a worker ranked higher, like a foreman.

clue.text: Rudolf is said to have pennies from heaven, dear

indicators.note: said signals that the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: pennies from heaven is a whimsical name for rain, followed by the word dear

explanation.surface: Rudolf talks of windfalls to a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf is Santa's red-nosed sleigh puller; 'Pennies from Heaven' is a song about rain, so RAIN DEAR said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf of the Christmas song is the red-nosed member of Santa's sleigh team of antlered deer.

parts.note: the playground saying finders ..., plus the guard ring worn to hold a wedding band on

explanation.surface: Who found the jewellery?
explanation.walkthrough: By 'finders keepers' the finder holds on to it; a guard ring that keeps a wedding ring in place also has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Finders are keepers by the old rhyme, and a guard band that holds a wedding ring on bears the name too.

clue.text: Two or three games supplied by stationer

definitions.meaning: in bridge or whist, a match of best of three games
an eraser sold in a stationery shop

explanation.surface: A few matches sold by an office-supplies shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a contest of best of three games has this name, settled in two or three.
explanation.definitionFit: A best-of-three bridge match carries this name, and so does a pencil eraser bought from a stationer.

parts.note: a ... climbs church towers and spires to repair them

explanation.surface: Where a man named Jack goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a person's name, or the Jack of the beanstalk; it completes steeplejack, whose job is climbing spires.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall church spire is what a steeplejack climbs for work.

clue.text: Kind of gamble is without point

parts.note: spec, short for speculation, is a gamble

indicators.note: without here means outside, so is goes round the point

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A sort of bet that has no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: IS goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological kind of organism, or any type or sort, is one sense of the word.

clue.text: What the florist does to these flowers ?

definitions.text: What the florist does to these flowers ?

parts.words: What the florist does to these flowers
parts.note: a florist keeps a supply of flowers on sale, and the scented garden flowers share the verb's name

explanation.surface: A question about a flower seller's handling of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower and the verb for keeping goods in supply are the same word, so the florist does this to these blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant garden flower shares its name with the verb for keeping goods in supply.

clue.text: Reverse car in the island race — easily managed

annotationWithheld.why: Reverse car in the island race — easily managed: T(RAC)T from car reversed inside TT gives TRACT, but no word of the clue as printed supplies ABLE
annotationWithheld.clue: Reverse car in the island race — easily managed

indicators.note: fracturing the word blame breaks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Blaming a broken bone for a horse's gait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracture' rearranges BLAME. 'mount' is a horse, not a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's easy walking gait is a relaxed pace for a mount.

clue.text: Desire no part of this temptress

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Want none of this seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these singers lured sailors to wreck, so any seductive woman bears the name.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
pica is a size of printing type

explanation.surface: A kind of southern celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type of star' reads as a kind; 'type' is printing type, PICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.

definitions.meaning: a heavy rope or chain used by one who tows a vessel

explanation.surface: A signal sent down from a castle keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' suggests a tall building; read it as tow-er, one who tows, using a stout rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent overseas by wire had this name, and so does the stout rope a towing ship uses.

clue.text: Get rid of priest in team, possibly

parts.note: Eli was the priest of Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of in team may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Dropping a clergyman from the side, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container word, but it is fodder: 'possibly' rearranges INTEAM to MINATE, after ELI.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove completely or knock out of a competition is to get rid of.

clue.text: Ways to get 'round little children's demands

indicators.note: the streets get round the little word, enclosing it

parts.note: STS is the abbreviation for streets, which are ways
wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: Methods of dodging what small kids ask for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get round' looks like 'evade'; here STS goes round WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Candies are what small kids keep asking for, their typical demands.

parts.note: to calumniate is to slander, to defame falsely

explanation.surface: A resident admitting to defamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives on an island is a type of resident.
